day_local: Ubluq Nalliunirsioqtaaqtuq Saint Elizabeth of Hungary-mik, Upalungaiqsimajuq
greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the peace of Christ, who stands at the door and knocks, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to open our hearts to your presence. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you invite us to dine with you in your kingdom. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you seek out the lost and bring them home. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.
homily:
We often think of the life of faith as a destination—a place we are trying to reach, a finish line we hope to cross if we just run fast enough. We imagine that if we do all the right things, if we keep our lives tidy and our records clean, we will eventually be invited into the presence of God. But look at the image the Lord gives us today in the Book of Revelation. He does not say, 'Come find me.' He says, 'Behold, I stand at the door and knock.'

Think of that for a moment. The Creator of the universe, the Amen, the faithful and true witness, is not waiting for us to climb a mountain to reach Him. He is the one moving toward us. He is the one standing at the threshold of our lives, waiting for the latch to lift. It is a posture of such profound humility, such desperate, beautiful patience. He is not a distant judge; He is a guest waiting to be invited in.

We see this same movement in the Gospel today with Zacchaeus. He was a man who knew what it was to be on the outside. He was short, he was a tax collector, and he was surrounded by a crowd that wanted nothing to do with him. He had to climb a sycamore tree just to get a glimpse of the passing Savior. He was trying to see Jesus, but he didn't realize that Jesus was already looking for him. 'Zacchaeus, come down quickly,' the Lord says, 'for today I must stay at your house.'

There is a theme here, a thread that runs through both readings: the hunger of God for the company of His people. Whether it is the Church in Laodicea being called to repentance or the tax collector in his tree, the Lord is always trying to bridge the gap. He wants to dine with us. He wants to sit at our table. He wants to be part of the ordinary, daily rhythm of our lives.

Benjamin knew something about this kind of invitation. Think of the way he lived, with that brilliant, curious mind always looking for the next horizon. He wasn't just a boy who loved math or technology; he was a boy who looked at the world with an open heart. He loved his 'con chim airlines'—that little dream of flight, that desire to see the world from above. It was a reflection of a soul that was always reaching, always wanting to see more, always wanting to be part of something bigger. And that, in the end, is what faith is. It is the willingness to look up, to climb the tree, to stand at the window and watch for the One who is coming.

Alan and Thao, I know the weight of the silence in the house. I know that for five months, you have been living in a space that feels empty where it should be full. But listen to the promise of the Lord: 'I will enter his house and dine with him, and he with me.' The Lord is not just a visitor in your home; He is a resident. He is there in the quiet moments when you remember the way Benjamin would greet his father every single morning without fail. He is there in the memories of the family trips, in the laughter of the brothers, in the moments of joy that still ripple through your lives. He is the one who is holding Benjamin, and He is the one who is holding you.

There is a temptation, when we carry a heavy cross, to think that we have failed, that we have missed a turn, or that we are being punished. But look at the Gospel again. Jesus does not go to the home of the righteous; He goes to the home of the sinner. He goes to the home of the one who is lost. He does not ask for perfection; He asks for an open door. He does not ask for a resume; He asks for a heart. You have nothing to fear from the Lord. He does not accuse you. He does not blame you. He only loves you with a love that is stronger than any sorrow you could ever carry. You have been faithful. Your love for your boy is a testament to the love of God Himself.

Ryan, my brother, you know better than anyone the heart of your brother. You know the way he looked at the world, the way he laughed, the way he cared. That bond you share is not a thing of the past. It is a living, breathing reality in the heart of God. When you feel the ache of his absence, remember that you are part of a 'perfect four' that is held together by the grace of Christ. Your brother is not gone; he is simply at the table where the Lord is serving. He is waiting for you, and he is cheering for you, and he is still, in his own way, walking by your side.

There is a beautiful, quiet truth in the way Benjamin lived. He was a boy who understood that the greatest thing you can do with your life is to give it away. Think of that moment when he offered his piggy bank to his uncle. He didn't have to do it. No one asked him to. He didn't even break the bank. The act itself was the point. It was the declaration of a boy who knew that everything he had—every coin, every dream, every hour of his life—was meant to be an offering. That is the spirit of the victor that the Book of Revelation speaks of. The victor is not the one who conquers the world; the victor is the one who gives himself away to the One who conquered death.

We must learn to live with our hands open, just as Benjamin did. We must learn to invite the Lord into our houses, even when those houses feel broken or quiet. We must learn to listen for the knock at the door. Sometimes, we hear it in the middle of the night when we are struggling to sleep. Sometimes, we hear it in the middle of the day when a memory of a smile or a shared laugh catches us off guard. That is the Lord. That is the Savior, standing at the door, asking to come in and share the bread of life with you.

To those of you who are watching from afar, who are carrying your own heavy crosses, who are wondering if your life has any meaning, look at the life of this young boy. Look at the way his love continues to flow, like the water from the well in Cà Mau. His life was not a tragedy; it was a mission. It was a life that touched the world, and it is a life that continues to touch the world through the kindness and mercy that he inspires in others. You, too, have a mission. You, too, have a life that is precious in the sight of God. You are not defined by your suffering; you are defined by the love that God has for you.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Carry the peace of the open door. Don't be afraid to let the Lord in. Don't be afraid to show Him your heart, even the parts that are broken, even the parts that are heavy with grief. He is the one who can heal the brokenhearted. He is the one who can turn your sorrow into joy. He is the one who is standing at the door, waiting to dine with you. And when you open it, you will find that you are not alone. You will find that you are home. And in that home, there is a place for you, and a place for your boy, and a place for all who have loved and lost, in the eternal banquet of the Father's love.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His light shine upon you always. Go in peace.
standing_petitions: For our dear Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's presence.
For all who carry the heavy burden of grief, that God may console them, strengthen their hearts, and fill them with the hope of eternal reunion.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text: I, John, heard the Lord saying to me: “To the angel of the Church in Sardis, write this: ‘The one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says this: “I know your works, that you have the reputation of being alive, but you are dead. Be watchful and strengthen what is left, which is going to die, for I have not found your works complete in the sight of my God. Remember then how you accepted and heard; keep it, and repent. If you are not watchful, I will come like a thief, and you will never know at what hour I will come upon you. However, you have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments; they will walk with me dressed in white, because they are worthy. The victor will thus be dressed in white, and I will never erase his name from the book of life but will acknowledge his name in the presence of my Father and of his angels. Whoever has ears ought to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.’” “To the angel of the Church in Laodicea, write this: ‘The Amen, the faithful and true witness, the source of God’s creation, says this: “I know your works; I know that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were either cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth. For you say, ‘I am rich and affluent and have no need of anything,’ and yet do not realize that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked. I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire so that you may be rich, and white garments to put on so that your shameful nakedness may not be exposed, and buy ointment to smear on your eyes so that you may see. Those whom I love, I reprove and chastise. Be earnest, therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will enter his house and dine with him, and he with me. I will give the victor the right to sit with me on my throne, as I myself first won the victory and sit with my Father on his throne. Whoever has ears ought to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text: R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne. He who walks blamelessly and does justice; who thinks the truth in his heart and slanders not with his tongue. R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne. Who harms not his fellow man, nor takes up a reproach against his neighbor; By whom the reprobate is despised, while he honors those who fear the LORD. R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne. Who lends not his money at usury and accepts no bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be disturbed. R. I will seat the victor beside me on my throne.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: At that time Jesus came to Jericho and intended to pass through the town. Now a man there named Zacchaeus, who was a chief tax collector and also a wealthy man, was seeking to see who Jesus was; but he could not see him because of the crowd, for he was short in stature. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree in order to see Jesus, who was about to pass that way. When he reached the place, Jesus looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, come down quickly, for today I must stay at your house.” And he came down quickly and received him with joy. When they saw this, they began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to stay at the house of a sinner.” But Zacchaeus stood there and said to the Lord, “Behold, half of my possessions, Lord, I shall give to the poor, and if I have extorted anything from anyone I shall repay it four times over.” And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house because this man too is a descendant of Abraham. For the Son of Man has come to seek and to save what was lost.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
